slides.title: How to get your book into bookstores in 2027
slides.answer: Bookstores order from wholesale catalogs, not from authors. Make your book **orderable** first: an ISBN under a publisher name, clean metadata and a listing with the wholesalers stores already use. Then make it **worth stocking**: terms the trade accepts and a reason for a store to believe its customers will buy it.

slides.title: How bookstores actually buy books
slides.lead: Bookstores order most of their books from wholesalers. One account covers thousands of publishers, with one invoice and fast delivery.

items.t: Booksellers search wholesale catalogs that list millions of titles. They do not browse author websites or answer cold emails.
A store buys below the list price, expects a trade discount and often the option to return unsold copies.
A self-published book reaches a bookstore the same way as any other: listed where booksellers order, on terms they accept.

slides.title: Where bookstores order in the US, the UK and Germany

items.t: Stores and libraries order through the catalogs of the major book wholesalers. Baker & Taylor announced in October 2025 that it would cease operations.
Wholesalers such as Gardners, which keeps about 500,000 titles in stock for same-day dispatch. Publishers register with Nielsen BookData.
Barsortimente – Libri, Zeitfracht and Umbreit – deliver overnight. Titles are looked up in the VLB, the directory of available books.

slides.title: Five things a bookstore needs from your book
slides.lead: Without the first three, the book cannot be ordered at all. Without the last two, it can be ordered but is unlikely to be stocked.
items: **An ISBN and a publisher name** – it identifies the edition and puts it into Books in Print
**Complete metadata** – title, author, format, price, date, subject categories
**Wholesale availability** – through the wholesaler the store already buys from
**A trade discount** – the store lives on the difference to the list price
**Returnability** – many booksellers only buy books they can send back

slides.title: Orderable is not the same as stocked
slides.text: Print on demand makes a book orderable wherever the wholesaler reaches. A store only puts copies on its shelf if it expects them to sell.
slides.source: Every copy on a shelf is money the store has already spent.

slides.title: Why most self-published books never reach the shelf

items.t: Traditional publishers bring sales reps, seasonal catalogs, advance copies and budgets. A self-published title usually arrives with none of these.
A book that is non-returnable or carries a short discount can be orderable, but the store takes all the risk on every copy.
A publisher the store knows, listed with its usual wholesaler, makes the yes much easier.
A customer asks, the store orders one copy, the customer picks it up: a real sale through a real bookstore.

slides.title: Make your book orderable
slides.lead: These three steps decide whether a bookseller can order your book at all.

items.h: Get an ISBN under a publisher name
items.t: The ISBN and the imprint travel with every record a bookseller sees. See [what a publishing imprint is](https://shelfpublisher.com/blog/what-is-a-publishing-imprint?utm_source=github&utm_medium=deck&utm_campaign=bookstores-2027).
Title, author, format, price, publication date and subject categories, in the directories of every market you sell in.
Stores order on the account they already have. If your book is not in that catalog, the usual way to order it does not exist.

slides.title: Make your book worth stocking
slides.lead: Being listed opens the door. These steps give a bookseller a reason to walk through it.

items.t: A real trade discount and returnable status are the first things a buyer asks about.

items.h: Give one store a local reason
items.t: A local subject, a reading, a signing or a talk turns a maybe into a few copies on display.

items.h: Send readers to ask for it
items.t: Every reader who asks for your book in a store brings it closer to the shelf.

slides.title: How to get your book into Barnes & Noble
slides.lead: What B&N's own help pages say, as of October 2026.

items.t: B&N lists titles from bibliographic data the publisher supplies: ISBN, title, author, publisher, format, price, date, BISAC and discount.
The record goes to B&N ideally at least 180 days before publication.
B&N states it will never offer in-store placement for your books in exchange for money.
Wholesale distribution under a publisher, listed in the catalogs B&N stores already order from.

slides.title: Consignment: what to get in writing first
slides.lead: The store takes a few copies without paying upfront and pays you for the ones that sell. Terms differ from store to store.
items: The split between you and the store
Any intake or handling fee
How long the books stay on display
How and when you are paid
What happens to damaged or unsold copies
Works best with a local subject, an event or a reading group

slides.title: How to pitch your book to a local bookstore

items.t: Ask who handles ordering. Bring a copy of the book.
ISBN, price, format, publisher, a short description and how the store can order it.
Booksellers notice who supports their store.
Discount, returnability and wholesaler are the first questions a buyer asks.
A reading, a signing or a talk gives the store a reason to stock and promote copies.
Shelf space is limited, and a store's decision about its own shelves is final.
A self-published book is found through its sales, and its reviews decide whether readers buy. With few reviews, one one-star rating pulls the average down.
A bookseller looks at the publisher, the ISBN, the price and the terms. No reviews or ad budget are needed for a store to order your book.

items.q: Do bookstores buy books directly from authors?
items.a: Usually not. Most stores order through wholesalers so they can buy many publishers' books on one account. Some independent stores take local authors' books on consignment.

items.q: Can a print-on-demand book be sold in bookstores?
items.a: Yes. Listed with a wholesaler, it can be ordered by any store that uses that wholesaler. Whether a store keeps copies on the shelf depends on the terms and expected demand.

items.q: Will bookstores put my book on their shelves?
items.a: Every store that orders from these catalogs can order it, for a customer or for its own shelf. What a store keeps on the shelf is the bookseller's choice.

items.q: How long until my book appears in stores?
items.a: With Shelf Publisher, usually about 8 to 9 days after you submit it, in most cases within two weeks; some retailers take longer.
